Buy & Hold: starting_capital divided equally across the universe (a real passive-investor allocation model).
assumptions_impact: Long-only scope reduction: DIRECTIONALLY UNKNOWN impact. 1-month formation period: MINOR, a direct restatement of the paper's own headline specification. Single-vintage holding (vs. the paper's overlapping-portfolio construction): MODERATE-to-MATERIAL, DIRECTIONALLY UNKNOWN -- identical reasoning to every prior cross-sectional strategy's own single-vintage deviation; note the much shorter holding period (1 month vs. 6 months) means meaningfully more trade turnover than the momentum strategies, a genuine behavioral difference worth weighing in the eventual portfolio-impact analysis, not just a weaker/stronger version of the same mechanism. Exit rule (21-trading-day time-stop only, no percentile-based early exit): N/A for the time-stop itself. Protective stop-loss (8%) and position sizing (1% risk/unit): MINOR by themselves, but structurally significant in that NEITHER exists in the source paper at all -- worth noting that buying stocks which just fell sharply places entries inherently closer (in percentage terms) to a plausible further-decline scenario than a momentum strategy's entries, though the SAME 8% convention is used regardless, disclosed as a point of interpretive difference, not a rule change.
